speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to begin my assessment, how long has this dizziness been lasting, and does it worsen when you move your head? Additionally, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or difficulty speaking alongside the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your description of the brief, sudden spinning sensation triggered by changing position, this pattern is highly suggestive of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Given your age and the specific duration, have you noticed any recent head trauma, or do you have a history of inner ear infections?

REQUEST TEST: Audiogram
